xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5588: Gate admission under sustained CPU pressure admits one gate per 10 minutes: CPU bypass bound restarts for every head

plan.title: Gate admission under sustained CPU pressure admits one gate per 10 minutes: CPU bypass bound restarts for every head
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Under sustained CPU pressure the quality-gate admission queue admits one gate per resources.quality_gate_cpu_bypass_minutes (default 10). cpuBlockedSince is per ticket and set only while the ticket is head, so every new head restarts the bound. With N waiters the last waits about N x 10 minutes for runs that take seconds (observed 2026-11-21 with 4 gates behind ffmpeg + OBS load).
narratives.Proposal: Make the CPU-pressure episode a property of the queue: a marker file cpu-blocked-since.json ({since}) in the admission root, written create-exclusive by the first head that records a CPU block. A head that has sampled pressure itself counts from min(own cpuBlockedSince, marker.since), so after one bypassed gate the next head starts alone as soon as the slots are empty. A head that has not sampled never uses the marker, so a stale marker plus a low sample is a normal admission. Only an unpressured admission of the queue head (position === 0, final return, after settle and memory re-check) deletes the marker, so a waiter that passes a memory-blocked head cannot end the episode; a cpuBypassed admission and every release keep it, so gates that arrive one after another under sustained pressure do not each wait the bound. Alone is kept (taken.size === 0). First extract the admission fs primitives to a leaf module so quality-gate-admission.ts stays under the 1000-line file-size ceiling. Full detail, before/after code and test sketches: .pan/drafts/PAN-5588.md. The CPU-bypass log lines now attribute the wait to the queue.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to the memory bypass (PAN-5285) or its 5-minute bound
- No change to slot counts, the PSI threshold, the bypass default, or config schema keys
- readQualityGateQueue() and the Flywheel page do not report the marker
- No marker heartbeat or age-based staleness rule beyond own-sample-first and clear-on-unpressured-admission
- release() never reads or deletes the marker (no clear when the queue goes idle)
- Non-head waiters never read or write the marker
- Never raise scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt
- Do not rename the '### CPU and memory admission (...)' heading in docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md (its anchor is linked)

autoDecisions.summary: A head uses the queue marker only after it has sampled pressure itself (own cpuBlockedSince set); cpuSince = min(own, marker).
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's step 2 taken literally lets a stale marker bypass a head that never sampled, contradicting the issue's own AC that a stale marker plus an unpressured sample admits normally. Cost is one extra 1 s poll per head.

autoDecisions.summary: The marker is deleted only by an unpressured admission; release() never touches it, even when the queue goes idle.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches issue steps 3 and 5. Clearing on an idle release was considered and rejected: a verification run's gates and an agent's tsc-then-vitest arrive one after another, so each would wait the full bound again. Accepted cost: a marker that outlives its episode lets the next episode's first head start alone after one pressured sample.

autoDecisions.summary: Extract the private fs primitives into src/lib/cloister/quality-gate-admission-files.ts before the feature change.
autoDecisions.rationale: quality-gate-admission.ts is 997 lines against a 1000-line ceiling with no allowlist row; exporting the helpers from the admission module instead would create an import cycle with quality-gate-cpu.ts.
It is the small CPU-rule module and the leaf files module keeps it free of an import cycle with quality-gate-admission.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: Change cpuBypassedMessage() and the validation.ts onLog line to attribute the bypass to the queue; keep the docs ### heading unchanged.
autoDecisions.rationale: Plan critique: a gate inheriting the episode did not itself wait the bound. The heading anchor is linked from docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md line 119.

autoDecisions.summary: Marker stores the injected now() value as {"since": <epoch ms>}; unparseable or non-positive values count as absent and are replaced.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the ticket's cpuBlockedSince clock so fake-clock tests are deterministic; mtime would not follow the injected clock.

autoDecisions.summary: Only the head's unpressured admission (position === 0) deletes the marker.
autoDecisions.rationale: Plan critique: a waiter passing a memory-blocked head could otherwise erase the marker while that head still bypasses on its own clock, restarting the bound for the next head. Matches PAN-5520's rule that only the head's admission ends its CPU clock.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3. In quality-gate-admission.ts: (1) markCpuBlocked also calls markQueueCpuBlocked(root, ticket.cpuBlockedSince) after persisting the ticket, so both the pre-settle and settle-time pressured paths write the marker. (2) Replace `const cpuSince = ticket.cpuBlockedSince` with: ownSince = ticket.cpuBlockedSince; queueSince = position === 0 && ownSince != null ? await readQueueCpuBlockedSince(root) : null; cpuSince = ownSince == null ? undefined : Math.min(ownSince, queueSince ?? Infinity). Keep the cpuAlone expression's position === 0 && taken.size === 0 terms. (3) Right after `await unlinkIfExists(ownTicketPath)` at the success return, add `if (!cpuAlone && position === 0) await clearQueueCpuBlock(root)`. (4) Rewrite the PAN-5520 paragraph of the module header per the PRD. Tests in describe('CPU bypass (PAN-5520)'): add a markerSince(rootDir) helper; rewrite 'keeps FIFO behind a CPU-blocked head, and counts the bound only for the head' so the second head resolves cpuBypassed with the clock unchanged after the first releases (it must fail under the old per-ticket code); add the slots-1 next-head, never-two-at-once, unpressured-clears-marker, stale-marker-low-sample cases and the settle-time marker assertion exactly as described in the PRD. Fake timers and injected now/samplePressure only; no skip/only/skipIf. Also add the sequential-arrival test: gate 1 bypassed and released, marker still {since:1}, only then gate 2 enqueues and resolves cpuBypassed at the unchanged clock. Do not add any marker handling to release(). Also add the memory-passer test from the PRD: a CPU-blocked head that becomes memory-blocked is passed by a small gate admitted on low samples, and the marker keeps since 1; the head later bypasses and the next gate inherits the episode.

items.title: Given sustained pressure and bound 1000, when the first head is admitted cpuBypassed at clock 2000 and released, then the next gate resolves cpuBypassed with the clock still at 2000 after sampling pressure at least once itself, both with slots 1 and in the rewritten slots-2 FIFO test (which contains no 'clock = 4_000' step and fails under the old per-ticket code)

Given sustained pressure, slots 2 and three gates, while one bypassed gate holds owner.json the others stay unsettled and slot-1.json never exists; each later gate is admitted only after the previous one releases

Given a marker {"since":1} and low samples, a gate is admitted with cpuBypassed false after at least 2 pressure samples and the marker file is deleted; a later gate under pressure from clock 10000 is still unsettled at clock 10900 and resolves cpuBypassed at clock 11100

When the first head records a CPU block at clock 1 (before or after the settle), cpu-blocked-since.json holds {"since":1}; given gate 1 admitted cpuBypassed and released before gate 2 enqueues, the marker preserves since 1 and gate 2 resolves cpuBypassed with the clock unchanged

Given a head that recorded a CPU block at clock 1 and then became memory-blocked, when a smaller later gate passes it and resolves with cpuBypassed false on low samples, then cpu-blocked-since.json still contains {"since":1}, and after the head bypasses and releases the next gate resolves cpuBypassed at the unchanged clock
